claims.text: Controlled processing can produce HfNbTaTiZr with low oxygen content.
The proposed initial HfNbTaTiZr material contains less than 1 wt.% oxygen.
The processed alloy is a single-phase random solid solution.
The alloy has measurable impurity-induced lattice distortions.
A coupled DFT/ML framework can model lattice and electronic thermal transport as separate channels.
An effective Debye spectrum modified by local disorder and impurity scattering can represent phonon transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local lattice distortions and oxygen-induced defect states separately alter phonon scattering rates and the electronic density of states.
Variations in atomic mass and force constants caused by chemical complexity and oxygen impurities modify the phonon spectrum and lattice thermal conductivity.
Explicitly separating phonon and electronic channels will improve predictive accuracy relative to ideal-crystal analytical approaches.
Below approximately 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are of similar magnitude.
Above approximately 300 K, lattice thermal transport dominates total thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen has total thermal conductivity between 10 and 17 W/(K·m) above approximately 300 K.
The proposed framework will reduce overall prediction error by approximately 30% relative to earlier analytical approaches.
The proposed approach is applicable from approximately 100 K to 1200 K for alloys with oxygen levels near or below 1 wt.%.
Significant impurity concentrations or secondary phases may invalidate the transport-channel decoupling assumption.
Magnetic-field perturbations or Lorenz-number analysis can experimentally separate lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in this alloy.
A deviation greater than ±25% between predicted and experimentally extracted channel contributions is designated as a falsifying outcome.
